text.empty: No hazards in this assessment yet.
text.catalogueNote: The eleven hazard-factor groups of the BAuA handbook on risk assessment, with typical examples for the kind of site chosen above. Pick one to fill the form, then write it for your own workplace.
text.measuresNote: For every hazard: measures in the STOP order (substitution, technical, organisational, personal), each with an owner, a due date and its status; once done, the check of whether it works; then the risk rated again as it is with the measures in place.
text.scalesNote: Rate the likelihood of the harm you rated, not of any incident: a fall from the dock is unlikely, a bruise from a roll cage is not. Rate the most likely serious outcome, as the work is done today.
text.reviewNote: Each assessment is reviewed on its date, and at once after an injury in the area, a near miss that could have been fatal, or a change (process, equipment, layout, substances, new or vulnerable people).
text.legal: This tool helps you carry out and document a risk assessment; it is not legal advice. It follows the German practice of the Gefährdungsbeurteilung: the Occupational Safety and Health Act (ArbSchG § 5 assess, § 6 document, § 4 measures with personal protection last, § 3 check that they work), the hazard factors of the BAuA handbook and the STOP order. Check the law where you work and involve your safety specialist: in Germany the Fachkraft für Arbeitssicherheit, the company doctor and the DGUV rules of your Berufsgenossenschaft; in Albania the law on safety and health at work (Law No. 10237/2010) and its by-laws.
text.legalShort: Not legal advice: check the law where you work with your safety specialist.

special.name: Young workers (under 18)
special.note: Assess their work separately: no work beyond their strength, with hazardous substances or high accident risk, unless training needs it and a competent person supervises (in Germany: JArbSchG §§ 22 and 28a).

special.name: Pregnant or breastfeeding workers
special.note: Assess every activity for them, whether or not anyone is pregnant now, and set the protective measures before a pregnancy is announced (in Germany: MuSchG § 10). Lifting, hazardous substances and working alone need a decision.

special.name: Workers with disabilities
special.note: Adjust the workplace, escape routes and alarms to the person (in Germany: ArbStättV § 3a (2)).

special.name: New starters and workers with little of the local language
special.note: Instruct them before they start, in a language they understand, and check that it was understood (in Germany: ArbSchG § 12).

groups.name: Mechanical hazards
groups.factors: Unguarded moving parts, moving transport and work equipment (forklifts, trucks, conveyors), uncontrolled moving parts, dangerous surfaces, slipping, tripping and falling, falling from height
groups.ref: Germany: BetrSichV § 3, ASR A1.8 traffic routes

warehouse: Collision between forklift and pedestrian at blind aisle ends
Truck pulls away from the dock during loading
Goods falling from racking
Tripping over stretch film and empty pallets
Caught in a nip point of the conveyor or sorter
hotel: Slipping on wet floors in the kitchen and bathrooms
Cuts from knives and broken glass
Falling from a ladder or step stool
Caught in the roller ironer in the laundry
delivery: Slipping or tripping on steps and kerbs while carrying
Struck by passing traffic while unloading at the roadside
Roll cage rolling off the tail lift
Trapped by the sliding or rear door of the van

warehouse: Damaged cables and plugs on chargers and scanners
Short circuit across battery terminals
Work on the control cabinet of the sorter
hotel: Faulty kettles and hair dryers in guest rooms
Damaged cables on cleaning machines
Water near sockets in the kitchen and spa
delivery: Charging cables of electric vans in the rain
Damaged extension leads at the station

groups.name: Hazardous substances
groups.factors: Skin contact, breathing in, swallowing, physical and chemical effects (fire, reactions)

warehouse: Battery acid (sulfuric acid) at the charging station
Leaking parcels with chemicals
Diesel exhaust from trucks at the dock
hotel: Cleaning and disinfection chemicals (skin, eyes, mixing)
Pool chemicals (chlorine)
Dishwasher detergents and descalers
delivery: Dangerous goods in parcels (lithium batteries, aerosols)
Exhaust fumes in the loading hall

groups.name: Biological agents
groups.factors: Infection by microorganisms, sensitising or toxic effects (mould)

warehouse: Rodent and bird droppings in storage areas
Mould on returns and damp goods
hotel: Used needles, blood and body fluids in rooms
Legionella in water systems and showers
Food handling (salmonella, norovirus)
delivery: Spoiled food parcels and contaminated packaging
Respiratory infections from contact with many people

groups.name: Fire and explosion hazards
groups.factors: Flammable solids, liquids and gases, explosive atmospheres, explosives
groups.ref: Germany: ASR A2.2 fire protection, GefStoffV

warehouse: Hydrogen released while charging forklift batteries
Lithium-ion batteries in parcels and in scanners
Fire load of stored cardboard and pallets
Escape routes blocked, fire doors wedged open
hotel: Fat fire in the kitchen
Guests smoking in their rooms
Lint in the laundry dryers
delivery: Charging e-bikes and e-vans indoors
Fuel stored at the station

groups.name: Thermal hazards
groups.factors: Hot or cold media and surfaces

warehouse: Hot surfaces of shrink-wrap and heat-seal machines
Frozen goods and cold-store surfaces
hotel: Hot fat, steam and ovens in the kitchen
Hot water and steam in the laundry
delivery: Hot engine parts and exhaust
Dry ice in cold-chain boxes

groups.name: Specific physical effects
groups.factors: Noise, ultrasound and infrasound, whole-body and hand-arm vibration, optical radiation (UV, laser), ionising radiation, electromagnetic fields, over- or under-pressure

warehouse: Noise from the sorter and conveyors
Whole-body vibration on forklifts over damaged floors
Laser of scanners and dimensioning systems
hotel: Noise in the dishwashing area
UV radiation for outdoor staff (pool, garden)
delivery: Whole-body vibration while driving
UV radiation and heat on summer tours

groups.name: Working environment
groups.factors: Climate (heat, cold, draughts), lighting, lack of oxygen, escape and traffic routes, signs, space to move, layout of the workplace, sanitary and break rooms
groups.ref: Germany: ArbStättV and the ASR (A3.4 lighting, A3.5 room temperature)

warehouse: Cold and draughts at open dock doors
Poor lighting in the aisles
Heat under the roof in summer
Traffic and escape routes blocked by goods
hotel: Heat in the kitchen and laundry
Poor lighting in corridors and stairwells
Cramped storerooms and linen rooms
delivery: Heat in the van in summer, cold in winter
Dark entrances and stairwells
No toilet on the route

groups.name: Physical load
groups.factors: Lifting, holding, carrying, pushing and pulling loads, forced postures, repetitive work, static and dynamic work combined
groups.ref: Germany: LasthandhabV, the key indicator methods (LMM) of the BAuA

warehouse: Lifting heavy parcels from the trailer floor
Repetitive handling at the sorter infeed
Forced postures picking from the bottom shelves
Pushing and pulling full roll cages
hotel: Making beds and turning mattresses
Pushing heavy housekeeping trolleys
Standing for hours at the front desk
delivery: Carrying heavy parcels up stairs
Getting in and out of the van many times a day
Lifting parcels from the van floor

groups.name: Psychological load
groups.factors: Work content and task, work organisation (time pressure, working hours, shifts), social relations, working environment, new forms of work

warehouse: Time pressure at peak (pick rates, scanner targets)
Night shifts and changing rotas
Monotonous work at one station
hotel: Aggressive or abusive guests
Night audit alone with the responsibility for the house
Split shifts and short-notice rota changes
delivery: Tight delivery windows and route targets
Conflicts with recipients
Stress in heavy traffic

groups.name: Other hazards
groups.factors: Hazards from people (violence, robbery), animals and plants, road traffic, working alone, and anything not covered above
groups.ref: Germany: DGUV Rule 112-139 for lone-worker alarms

warehouse: Working alone in the charging room or at night
Theft and violence at the gate
External truck drivers who do not know the site rules
hotel: Robbery or violence at the night desk
Working alone in technical rooms
Intruders in staff areas
delivery: Road traffic accidents on the route
Dog attacks at the door
Working alone on the route, no help after an accident
Robbery of cash or valuable parcels

likelihood: Practically never: not expected in years of this work, here or elsewhere.
Could happen, but not known here; perhaps once in several years.
Has happened in similar work or here before; about once a year.
Happens here now and then; several times a year.
Expected: happens often, monthly or more, if nothing changes.
severity: No injury, or a minor one that needs no first aid.
First aid or a doctor's visit, back at work within three days.
Injury or illness with more than three days off (in Germany a reportable accident), fully recovered.
Serious or lasting injury, occupational disease, long absence.
Death, or several people seriously injured.

low.name: Low
low.meaning: Acceptable as it is. Keep the measures in place and look at it again at the next review.
moves: Check at the next walk that the existing measures are still in place.
Keep the hazard on the list, so a change in the work brings it back.
Use the instruction to keep people aware of it.
low.question: What would have to change for this risk to grow?

medium.name: Medium
medium.meaning: Measures are needed: plan them with an owner and a date, and bring the risk down as far as reasonably possible.
moves: Plan at least one measure above P in the STOP order, with an owner and a date.
Agree how and when the effect will be checked.
Rate the residual risk once the measure is in place.
medium.question: Which measure would make this hazard go away, not just make it less likely?

high.name: High
high.meaning: Measures are needed soon, before the work goes on as usual: look first for substitution and technical measures.
moves: Put an interim measure in place this week and the lasting one with a fixed date.
Ask whether the hazard can be removed or the work done another way (S) before guarding it (T).
Instruct everyone exposed and check the effect within a month.
high.question: Why is this hazard here at all, and who decided that it has to be?

very-high.name: Very high
very-high.meaning: Do not carry on as it is: stop or restrict the work until measures have brought the risk down.
moves: Stop or restrict the work now and tell the responsible manager and the safety specialist.
Agree the measures that must be in place before the work starts again.
Rate the risk again with the measures in place, and only then release the work.
very-high.question: What has to be true before anyone does this work again?

S.name: Substitution
S.hint: Remove the hazard or replace it: another substance, process, machine or way of working that is less dangerous.

T.name: Technical
T.hint: Deal with the hazard at its source and separate people from it: guards, barriers, interlocks, ventilation, lifting aids.

O.name: Organisational
O.hint: Change how the work is organised: rules, routes, rotation, rotas, permits, training and instruction, distance in time or space.

P.name: Personal
P.hint: Personal protective equipment and personal behaviour. It comes last, when S, T and O are not enough, and it needs instruction and checks.

signatures: Safety specialist (and company doctor where needed)
tips: One assessment per area or activity.
Where the work is the same, one assessment covers every workplace like it (ArbSchG § 5 (2)). A parcel hub needs a few: dock, traffic, picking, the charging room.
Walk it, with the people who do the work.
Hazards are found on the floor, not at the desk. Take one or two people from the shift and the safety specialist, and go through the eleven groups of the catalogue.
Rate it as it is today.
Likelihood and severity of the harm with the measures that are really in place, not the ones planned. The residual risk is rated separately, after the measures.
S before T before O before P.
Personal protective equipment comes last. A high risk met with gloves and a vest alone is flagged: look for a way to remove the hazard or keep people away from it first.
A measure is not finished when it is done.
Check that it works, on a date, and write down the result: that is what the law means by documenting the effectiveness check.
After an accident or a near miss, a new machine or layout, new substances or new people, and at the latest on the review date.

assessments.activity: Loading and unloading trucks and swap bodies (parcels in roll cages and on pallets)
assessments.assessor: Marco (shift lead) with the safety specialist
assessments.note: Walked the dock with two drivers of the late shift; carrier drivers were asked about the drive-away risk.

hazards.text: Truck pulls away during loading: forklift or pallet truck falls between dock and trailer

measures.text: Vehicle restraint or wheel chocks at every door; the dock light turns green only when the truck is secured
Drivers hand the truck key in at the gate office until loading is finished

hazards.text: Pedestrians crossing the dock behind reversing trucks and forklifts

measures.text: Painted pedestrian lane and barrier along docks 1–6
Nobody crosses a dock lane without eye contact with the driver; banksman when reversing
High-visibility vests for everyone on the dock, carrier drivers included

hazards.text: Lifting heavy parcels (up to 31.5 kg) from the trailer floor

measures.text: Extendable belt conveyor into the trailer for loose-loaded parcels
Two-person lift above 25 kg; heavy parcels marked at the sorter

hazards.text: Cold and draughts at the open dock doors in winter

measures.text: Dock shelters at doors 1–6
Winter jackets, gloves and thermal underwear issued in October

assessments.activity: Forklift and pallet-truck traffic in the aisles and cross-dock lanes
assessments.assessor: Luca (warehouse lead) with the safety specialist

hazards.text: Collision between forklift and pedestrian at blind aisle ends

measures.text: Blue-spot warning lights on all forklifts, convex mirrors at the aisle ends
Marked walkways; speed limit 6 km/h in the aisles
Only trained drivers with written authorisation; instruction once a year

hazards.text: Goods falling from racking (overhanging pallets, wrong stacking height)

measures.text: Racking inspected by a competent person every year; rack protection at the aisle ends
Maximum stacking height marked on each rack and checked twice a shift

hazards.text: Tripping over stretch film and empty pallets in the aisles

measures.text: Bins for stretch film at every aisle end
One aisle owner per shift signs the floor off before leaving

hazards.text: Whole-body vibration when driving over damaged floor joints and dock plates

measures.text: Repair the floor joint at cross-dock lane 2

assessments.activity: Picking and sorting parcels and small goods at the shelving and the sorter infeed
assessments.assessor: Anna (shift lead) with the company doctor
assessments.note: Two apprentices under 18 work in picking: their tasks were assessed with them.

hazards.text: Repetitive lifting and twisting at the sorter infeed

measures.text: Height-adjustable infeed tables and roller slides at the chutes
Rotation every two hours between infeed, picking and packing
Lifting-technique training with the company doctor

hazards.text: Forced postures when picking from the bottom and top shelves

measures.text: Step stools with a handrail in every aisle
Heavy and fast-moving items between knee and shoulder height (re-slotting)

hazards.text: Time pressure at peak (pick rates, scanner targets) and night work

measures.text: Peak staffing plan with temporary workers booked two weeks ahead
Breaks fixed in the shift plan and not skipped at peak

hazards.text: Poor lighting in aisles 10–14 (lamps out, shadows on the labels)

measures.text: Replace the lamps with LED and measure the lighting at the picking face

assessments.activity: Charging and changing lead-acid forklift batteries
assessments.assessor: Marco with the safety specialist and the battery supplier
assessments.note: Pregnant or breastfeeding workers do not work in the charging room (sulfuric acid, lifting).

hazards.text: Hydrogen released while charging: explosive atmosphere if the ventilation fails

measures.text: Ventilation to EN IEC 62485-3 with an airflow monitor that stops charging
No smoking, no open flame, no sparks: signs at the door, hot work only with a permit

hazards.text: Acid splashes (sulfuric acid) when topping up water or handling batteries

measures.text: Face shield, acid-resistant gloves and apron

hazards.text: Short circuit across the battery terminals (a tool on the battery): arc and burns

measures.text: Only instructed staff charge and change batteries
Insulated tools only; rings and watches off

hazards.text: Crushing when changing batteries (up to 1.5 t)

measures.text: Battery-change trolley with roller bed and end stops

hazards.text: Working alone in the charging room on the night shift

measures.text: Personal emergency alarm for lone work
Lone-worker check-in with the shift lead every 30 minutes
